title: Batch-silence snowball analysis and hardening
creator: Aisha Patel
description: A production capacity event on 2026-02-14 triggered a cascading ‘batch-silence’ that amplified tail latency and produced fairness regressions across several serving pools. Small increases in eviction pressure in the KV cache combined with a surge of long-sequence requests caused repeated batch formation stalls on a subset of GPUs. The incident manifested as prolonged token-generation pauses (100–600ms microfreezes) for medium-priority requests and a 3–6x tail latency increase for affected routes. This ticket captures the incident analysis, short-term mitigations deployed, and proposed hardening work to prevent recurrence.

root_cause: A confluence of sub-threshold KV cache eviction bursts and a short-duration surge of long-context requests created a feedback loop: evictions increased prefix cache misses, which lengthened per-request token generation and delayed coalescer timers. The continuous batcher’s windowing heuristics and affinity slots then became temporarily dominated by these long requests, causing other queues to starve (priority inversion) and producing intermittent batch formation silence on several workers.
decision_log: Accept short-term conservative throttles to restore fairness (deployed 2026-02-14).
Reject immediate full disable of KV eviction (would blow memory budgets); instead pursue targeted gating and shadow-warming.
Prioritize slot-level isolation and preemptive micro-throttles over coarse pool scaling for long-term fix.

mitigation_playbook: Short-term (already applied): conservative preemption for best-effort routes; scale bump for affected pools; lowered max-inflight-tokens per slot.
Medium-term: slot-level eviction gating (prevent whole-slot eviction waves) + staggered eviction windows to avoid synchronized cache pressure.
Long-term: affinity-aware KV shadow-warming + coalescer timer sensitivity tuning; adjust batching heuristics to detect and rebalance long-request dominance.
Runbook items: signal detection rules for batch-silence (sustained drop in batches formed per second + rising per-request token time) and automated temporary throttles.
Post-deploy verification: canary on 2% traffic for 24h with synthetic mixed workload and monitor 99.9p latency and fairness ratio metrics.
